name: sar-logic-timing-gates-ok
description: Single-loop gate-level replay of the `ok` (0 ns delay, reference) loop of sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ -- the SAME gate-level timing-margin/cadence claim (README.md#target-specification, issue #11's synchronous-SAR timing-margin verification, DR-0008), against the SYNTHESIZED gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist (design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/netlist/sar_ctrl.mcu7t5v0.synth.v, issue #272), split out of the original five-loop deck by issue #311 because the five loops sharing one ngspice global timestep made the full 45-point mos grid unaffordable (sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/investigations/20260917-issue-303-five-loop-composition-cost.md) -- see that experiment's own testbench/ for the still-committed, unmodified five-loop deck kept for the nominal-PVT cross-check.
claim: README.md#target-specification -- Latency/conversion-timing row and the per-cycle timing budget in spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2, re-checked on the real synthesized gate netlist with NO added comparator-to-latch delay (the `ok` reference point), plus DR-0014's acquisition-window/isolation-gap timing (acq_window_ns/iso_gap_ns) and the sync cadence claim (ok_conv_period_ns, spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3).
netlist_provenance: schematic (gate-level, single-loop `ok`: klt-synthesized gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist wrapping sar_ctrl.v, issue #272 -- not yet placed-and-routed; DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c) own P&R/STA; split from the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck by issue #311's per-loop decomposition)

abs_err_delay_0ns.description: Reference -- UNCHANGED bound, carried over from the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck (issue #311). With no added decision delay, every conversion in the run must still be exact on the real gate netlist.

ok_conv_period_ns.description: Cadence on the undisturbed loop -- UNCHANGED bound. drdy must keep arriving exactly 16 clocks apart on real gf180mcu logic.

acq_window_ns.description: DR-0014 ACQUISITION WINDOW -- bound REVISED by DR-0028 (spec/decision-records/DR-0028-gate-level-acquisition-isolation-bounds.md, issue #319) from the inherited 187.3..188.0 ns. That pair was set by rounding the rung-1 ideal deck's SINGLE tt/27C measurement (187.625 ns, sim/sar-logic-timing/records/20260802-102758-d8a363d.md) taken on an XSPICE model with fixed T_CLK_Q/T_GATE placeholders and no process axis at all, then copied unchanged into this manifest; it appears in no spec file and no decision record. THE LIMITS HERE ARE DERIVED FROM THE MARGIN, NOT FROM A MEASUREMENT. LOWER LIMIT 175.0 ns = the settling floor: DR-0013's input-pin redistribution kick is 1024*C_in/(C_in+C_pin) = 83.06 LSB at the worst permitted C_pin = 100 pF, recovered with tau_in <= 30 ns (DR-0013's contract ceiling), so allocating 0.25 LSB -- half the 1/2-LSB settling criterion, to keep the term negligible rather than merely legal -- to the un-recovered residual at the sampling instant requires 30*ln(83.06/0.25) = 174.17 ns, rounded UP so the limit is never looser than its derivation. (NOT DR-0001's t/tau >= ln(2^11) = 7.62 full-scale-step rule, which would demand 228.6 ns: DR-0013 supersedes DR-0001 precisely by replacing the full-scale-step model with the pinned-capacitor one, in which the pin never takes a full-scale step.) UPPER LIMIT 218.7 ns = DR-0003's 4-clock sample phase (4 x 62.5 = 250 ns) less iso_gap_ns's 31.25 ns ordering floor, rounded DOWN. acq_window_ns + iso_gap_ns is measured at 250.09..250.50 ns at all 45 PVT points of 20260918-233547-1d81aa1, i.e. the sel_in_n pulse IS that 250 ns phase everywhere, so these two measurements are ONE degree of freedom and each upper limit is the other measurement's floor restated. LAYOUT-INDEPENDENT: every input (DR-0013's tau_in/C_pin contract, DR-0003's 62.5 ns phase, the 1/2-LSB criterion) is a spec quantity P&R does not change, so this is one limit pre- AND post-layout, not a pre-layout number to be re-baselined. Worst slack measured to date, PRE-LAYOUT: 1.93 ns at fs_125c_2.97v (176.927 ns, sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/records/20260918-233547-1d81aa1.md) -- thin, and deliberately so: P&R/extraction (#274/#275) is a real test of this floor, and breaking it there would be a genuine design-closure finding, not another widening.

iso_gap_ns.description: DR-0014's TWO-PHASE SAMPLE: the isolation gap, and its SIGN is the ordering claim -- bound REVISED by DR-0028 (issue #319) from the inherited 62.2..62.8 ns, which has the same idealised single-corner origin as acq_window_ns above. LOWER LIMIT 31.3 ns = the ordering floor, half of one DR-0003 clock phase (31.25 ns, rounded UP). POSITIVE means sel_in_n falls LAST -- the input legs turn off onto an already-isolated node, which is the entire mechanism of DR-0014 -- and both real failure modes are a whole clock phase in size (second phase DROPPED -> 0 ns; the two phases SWAPPED -> -62.5 ns), so a half-phase floor still fails decisively on both, by 31.25 ns and 93.75 ns. It leaves 22.0 ns beyond the worst PVT excursion measured (53.3104 ns at sf_125c_2.97v, 9.19 ns below the 62.5 ns nominal) -- 2.4x that excursion -- as headroom for P&R interconnect skew, extracted parasitics and on-die mismatch, none of which this pre-layout netlist has. UPPER LIMIT 75.0 ns = the 250 ns sample phase less acq_window_ns's 175.0 ns settling floor: excess isolation is missing acquisition, and by the sum invariant noted above this ceiling IS that floor restated. LAYOUT-INDEPENDENT, for the same reason as acq_window_ns. Worst slack to date, PRE-LAYOUT: 22.0 ns on the floor, 1.67 ns on the ceiling (73.3269 ns at fs_125c_2.97v, same record). The asymmetry is the finding: input settling is the binding constraint on the two-phase sample, and the ordering claim itself is robust across the whole PVT box.

notes: ISSUE #311 PER-LOOP DECOMPOSITION: this experiment is one of five (`sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/-lt/-xl/-bad/-tie`) split out of the single five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck. The measurement definitions, bounds and 8.5 us duration are UNCHANGED; only how many loops share one ngspice deck changed. Rationale, the cost measurement that motivated it, and the 'five slugs vs one deck-variant axis' decision are in sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/investigations/20260917-issue-303-five-loop-composition-cost.md and design/sar-logic/flow/gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's own module docstring ('Per-loop timing decomposition (issue #311)').

COMPUTATIONAL COST, MEASURED: the `ok` loop alone completes the full ratified 8.5 us transient in ~132 core-s (tt/27C/3.30V, SPARSE 1.3, num_threads=1) -- about 100x cheaper per simulated ns than the five-loop deck's own measured rate over its comparable early window (same investigation note above). This is the number that makes the full 45-point mos grid tractable for this claim, where the five-loop deck's was not.

CROSS-CHECK: this split deck's measurements are expected to agree with the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck's own `ok_*`/`acq_window_ns`/`iso_gap_ns` measurements at the same PVT point, to the solver's tolerance -- both instantiate byte-identical loop SPICE (design/sar-logic/gen_sar_logic.py's `_loop('ok', ...)`), differing only in how many OTHER loops share the deck. A record here states whether that cross-check was actually run and what it found; if a full five-loop run at nominal PVT could not be afforded, the record says so rather than asserting equivalence (issue #311 acceptance criteria).

The behavioural CDAC/comparator model, comparator output slew fix (issue #296, `cmp_out_rc`) and start-pulse seeding (design/sar-logic/rtl/README.md's 'Real hardware note') are all UNCHANGED from the five-loop deck -- only the loop composition changed.

What this record does NOT claim: no place-and-route, no STA/timing closure (DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c), issues #274/#275) -- this is a pre-layout gate-level netlist wrapped directly in SPICE, with no extracted parasitics and no real interconnect delay. It is also not evidence about real CDAC settling or comparator behaviour.
